newsitem.title: ITALY: Vranitzky says mission to Albania is vital.
newsitem.headline: Vranitzky says mission to Albania is vital.

text.p: European mediator Franz Vranitzky said on Wednesday that a multinational force was vital for Albania but it had to avoid the sort of mistakes made in former Yugoslavia.

Vranitzky, addressing a news conference in Rome before travelling to Athens to meet Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino and Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo, said the Italian-led force could be ready in 10 to 14 days.
"The Albanians need international help," Vranitzky, envoy to Albania of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), said after meeting Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini.
"It is of utmost importance that we coordinate our various activities in order to avoid what unfortunately happened in the Yugoslav crisis at the beginning," the former Austrian chancellor added.

He said the international community lacked agreement on objectives early on in the crisis in Albania's Balkan neighbour. "We have a chance as far as Albania is concerned to avoid the mistakes and the errors committed," he said.
The measures must restore public order in the country, rebuilding the shattered economy and restoring faith in the political system to enable elections to be held.
"There has to be an election this year," he said.

Dini said the time was right for the force and he and Vranitzky were in full agreement on the steps to be taken. "We have the full conviction that the protection force is indispensable to channel aid and protect citizens."
Italian opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said he was confident his centre-right bloc would back the plans to send soldiers when it came to a vote in parliament.

Preparations for the multinational force, which aims to protect humanitarian aid supplies by securing ports and Tirana airport, have been overshadowed by a wave of anti-Italian feeling in Albania after a fatal ship sinking on Friday.

More than 80 Albanians, mostly from the southern port of Vlore, were feared dead in the disaster which followed a collision with an Italian navy ship under orders to persuade Albanian vessels to turn away from Italian waters.
Dini, asked about Italian media reports that Rome had decided not to send troops to Vlore for security reasons, said that no such decision had been taken.

"The meeting today of high-ranking officials from the different countries will decide where the different forces will be deployed," he said. "I don't think we will suggest not going to the southeast. It will be a collective decision."
Military experts from countries willing to contribute troops were meeting in Rome for initial planning talks.
Dini said that after emotional scenes in Vlore in recent days, signs were emerging of a change in feeling in Albania.
"Yesterday there were clear signals coming out that Italian troops would be well received in Vlore itself," he said.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi flew to the rebel-held southern Albanian town of Gjirokaster early on Wednesday to meet Fino. He reaffirmed plans for the force and said Italy would give assistance to the families of the ship victims.
He also told Albania it would try to raise the wreck which Tirana says could hold dozens of bodies.
